niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You Freeze Before Starting Work
ideas.angle: Explains the psychological phenomenon of task paralysis and the amygdala hijacking your prefrontal cortex when an ambition feels ambiguous, revealing the counter-intuitive 2-minute fix that tricks the brain into action.
ideas.reason: Executive dysfunction and task freezing are currently experiencing massive viral engagement across TikTok and YouTube Shorts under burnout and ADHD-adjacent discourse, consistently earning high retention due to immediate self-identification.
sources: Ferrari, J. R. (2010). Still Procrastinating: The No-Regrets Guide to Getting It Done
Pychyl, T. A. (2013). Solving the Procrastination Puzzle

ideas.title: Why Small Talk Drains Your Battery
ideas.angle: Reveals that small talk triggers cognitive friction because your brain expends energy calculating social masks and shallow scripts rather than engaging the default mode network involved in genuine human connection.

hook.en: Why does small talk feel exhausting?

ideas.reason: Social fatigue and the 'social battery' concept dominate evergreen short-form psychology feeds, particularly among Gen Z and millennial audiences looking for clinical validation of everyday social friction.
sources: Mehl, M. R., et al. (2010). Eavesdropping on Happiness: Well-being is Related to Having Less Small Talk and More Substantive Conversations. Psychological Science
Kahneman, D. (2011). Thinking, Fast and Slow

ideas.title: Why You Suddenly Wake Up at 3 AM
ideas.angle: Demystifies the universal midnight panic wake-up by showing how the 3 AM cortisol surge pairs with low blood sugar to make small worries feel like life-or-death emergencies.

hook.en: Ever wake up panicking at three?

ideas.reason: Midnight awakening and catastrophizing affect millions daily; explaining the physiological mechanism behind sudden existential dread provides immediate relief and triggers strong share-to-friends loops.
sources: Walker, M. (2017). Why We Sleep: Unlocking the Power of Sleep and Dreams
Russell, G., & Lightman, S. (2019). The human circulating ultradian rhythm of cortisol. Frontiers in Neuroendocrinology
